title: Ozone sites had 54.5-69.4% positive agreement on days above 70 ppb before selected four-state bird surveys in 2005-2019
abstract: We tested agreement between the nearest two ozone sites within 50 km of bird route starts. We used 1,599 selected survey windows in California, Oregon, New York, and Pennsylvania in 2005-2019. Each window had at least 24 common valid days in the month before the survey. Positive agreement on days above 70 ppb was 54.5-69.4% across two regions and two periods. Only 1.4-5.0% of all paired days had different high-day status, because most days were below the threshold. Mean absolute gaps in monthly mean daily maximum ozone were 2.61-4.50 ppb. A 25-km limit raised positive agreement to 58.5-77.8%. Strict day coverage and equal route or site-pair weights did not remove disagreement. Only 31-55% of filtered surveys had the required two-site support. Selected surveys had warmer starts. This is a finite-sample exposure audit. Neither site is a true bird-exposure measure. Shared sites, selected roadside routes, missing days, and unknown site changes limit inference. We do not estimate bird damage or climate effects. The package has source hashes, raw-data rebuilds, common-day evidence, code, figures, and independent arithmetic checks.

display.caption: Agreement and absolute exposure gaps in four selected samples. All comparisons use common dates. Positive agreement excludes dates low at both sites. Three-day gaps are differences in scaled observed fractions, not imputed counts.
Positive agreement and high-day count gaps under stricter distance, stricter day coverage, equal site-pair weights, and equal route weights. All are descriptive selected-sample summaries.
